subject.title: Session→model/runtime binding drift persists across doctor --fix --deep because the repair's provider-ownership registry is missing the literal id "openai"

question: Should canonical `openai` session route state be owned for doctor cleanup by a new OpenAI provider doctor contract, by the Codex app-server contract, or by a generic provider-state repair path?
rationale: Literal `openai` is both the canonical OpenAI provider id and part of the current Codex app-server routing story, so automation should not choose the long-term provider ownership boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: OpenAI owns canonical provider state
options.body: Add an OpenAI-side doctor owner for `providerIds: ["openai"]` and test stale auto OpenAI route cleanup separately from legacy Codex aliases.

options.title: Codex owns the app-server route
options.body: Add `openai` to the Codex doctor owner if maintainers consider OpenAI agent turns primarily owned by the Codex app-server route.

options.title: Make auto cleanup generic
options.body: Move stale auto override cleanup into provider-agnostic doctor logic when the configured route no longer includes the override provider.

recommendation.title: OpenAI owns canonical provider state
recommendation.body: Add an OpenAI-side doctor owner for `providerIds: ["openai"]` and test stale auto OpenAI route cleanup separately from legacy Codex aliases.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior merged doctor/Codex route-state repair work makes this the clearest available owner-boundary decision path.
